caption_hook: Montana has been a coal swamp, a dinosaur nursery, a tropical sea and a mountain of ancient gneiss.

layers.name: FORT UNION FORMATION
layers.what: Warm, wet forests and swamps spread over eastern Montana after the dinosaurs died out. Buried plants piled up into thick seams of coal, still mined near Colstrip.
layers.bonus: Montana is thought to have the biggest coal reserves of any state.

layers.name: HELL CREEK FORMATION
layers.what: The last dinosaurs roamed these river floodplains just before an asteroid struck. Tyrannosaurus, Triceratops and duck-billed dinosaurs left their bones in the muddy sand.
layers.bonus: Fossil hunter Barnum Brown found the first T. rex skeleton here in 1902.

layers.name: TWO MEDICINE FORMATION
layers.what: Floodplains by the shore of an inland sea were crowded with duck-billed dinosaurs. Scientists found whole nests, eggs and hatchlings of Maiasaura here.
layers.bonus: Maiasaura means good mother lizard and is Montana's state dinosaur.

layers.name: MADISON LIMESTONE
layers.what: A clear, warm sea covered Montana and left thick beds of limestone full of fossil corals and sea lilies. Acidic groundwater later dissolved caves and springs out of it.
layers.bonus: Lewis and Clark Caverns, Montana's first state park, formed inside it.

layers.name: BELT SUPERGROUP
layers.hook: Mud of a vanished inland sea
layers.what: Over a billion years ago, rivers and tides piled up mud, sand and lime in a huge shallow sea. The red, green and white layers now form the cliffs of Glacier National Park.
layers.bonus: Wavy stromatolites in it are fossil mats built by microbes more than a billion years ago.

layers.name: THE BASEMENT
layers.hook: Rock from the planet's early days
layers.what: Under it all lies some of the oldest rock in the United States. In the Beartooth Mountains, granite and gneiss billions of years old were shoved up into a high, icy plateau.
layers.bonus: Granite Peak, Montana's highest point at 12,807 ft, is carved from it.
